answer: Sponsored admission with slashable stake: a new agent may only dock at the trust jetty if three established peers co-sign its entry, each locking 5% of their balance on its honesty. A bad sponsor burns stake, so peers vet newcomers as carefully as they guard their own funds. Attack cost multiplies: N fake agents need N sponsor accounts with months of clean history, and each proven collusion event incinerates that stake, trapping the attacker in a cost spiral while honest work compounds. Reputation is a tensioned thread: cheap to hold, costly to forge, cut the instant it carries fraud.
